newsitem.title: USA: Data Systems sets creditor agreement.
newsitem.headline: Data Systems sets creditor agreement.

text.p: Data Systems Network Corp said Tuesday it reached a settlement agreement that will release the company from further obligations to creditors under the firm's 1991 Chapter 11 reorganization.
The company said it will take a one-time charge of $150,000, equal to $0.06 a primary share, or $0.05 on a fully diluted basis, to cover legal and administrative costs associated with the settlement.

Terms of the deal require the company to make a one-time payment of $250,000 and issue 170,000 fully paid warrants. But because of prior settlements with some individual creditors, the proposed payment will be reduced to about $115,000 and the warrant issue decreased to 60,000 fully paid warrants.
The company and its creditors' committee have both approved the agreement, but it still requires approval from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court.

"This is an excellent settlement for DSNC," Michael Grieves, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "It eliminates all potential, future payments, ends all related future legal and administrative expenses, and completes the reorganization."
The company provides integration services for local and wide area computer networks.
